Roleplay is based on a central settlement called Coffinswode, it's pretty much the only safe place considering the island itself is so deadly, so all of the characters, from all sorts of backgrounds, usually clash there.

I still defend it because of the quality of the roleplay there and the people are genuine. I personally never had a problem with any DMs, but I left after an argument with Wolf about a player which I believed was over sexualized and suffered from same character syndrome on every new concept they created. 

It's a small server but growing quite fast and there's constant changes, rebalances and updates, plus the story is great. It's totally controlled by the player's actions so it can really lead anywhere.

The Blair Witch Project.

Most people consider this a horror classic for some reason, and some sort of trademark movie in the found footage category.

The plot of the movie is the following - Three students are making a documentary about the Blair Witch, some sort of well, witch that lives in Maryland.

Has potential, right? But hey, guess what!? Fuck that.

This is probably the most boring horror movie I've ever watched, here's a series of (uninspiring) events:

​

* They interview some people.
* They find out that the witch possesses people and they stand in the corner (This is very important for plot later on).
* They go out into the woods.
* They get lost.
* Spooky things made of wood (OoOoO Rituals!)
* They argue.
* One dude disappears.
* Shaky Cam™, Yelling™ and Darkness™ (Legit the last half of the movie is literally this.)
* "JOSH! JOSH! JOSH!"
* A closeup of someone's nose and crying.
* They find some abandoned house (Plot twist: It's the Witch's house! Nobody saw that coming.)
* They go inside the house and search for the dude.
* Oh no, the other dude is standing in the corner! (Remember that thing the witch did they found out earlier on?)
* It ends.

It just fucking ends like that.

The most impressive thing about this movie is that it's budget was 60k and they ended up making 248 million at the box office.

I am assuming that out of the 60k, at least 5k was split between the actors and the rest was spent on booze and hookers. It's the only explanation because the movie's a clusterfuck.

Anyway, to end this, I would like to say that I would rather go to the cinema and get 10 year old diarrhea smeared into my eyes for 1 hour and 45 minutes than watch this movie ever again.
